top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Black Friday’s Canucks Rundown will preview the game against the Philadelphia Flyers and provide a practice facility update. top.title: Kovač puts Gadou hype into perspective after Arsenal heroics
top.description: Kovač puts Gadou hype into perspective after Arsenal heroics Following his summer move from RB Salzburg, Joane Gadou has quickly established himself as a regular starter at the heart of Borussia Dortmund's defence. Most recently, the 19-year-old delivered a standout performance in Wednesday's 1-1 draw with Arsenal, earning widespread praise and sparking reports that a number of top European clubs are keeping tabs on him. Dortmund head coach Niko Kovač, too, is pleased with Gadou's development, but is keen to stress that the youngster still has plenty to learn. "I've said it time and time again: learning week after week in the Bundesliga is one thing, but the learning experience of playing against the best in the world in this sport every three days is many times greater," Kovač said at a press conference on Friday. "He is developing well and, like everyone else, still has areas where he can improve. But it would be far too easy if we were to say that he was already the finished article. He's not. But where he is at the moment, he is helping us a great deal. "He will be given all the time in the world and all the support he needs. He works hard at learning, and I like that. When you're learning, you're allowed to make mistakes too." Gadou has made 17 appearances for Dortmund so far this season.

top.title: Artemis III astronauts meet their spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 27, 2026
top.description: null NASA's Artemis III astronauts pose holding up three fingers to symbolize their mission as they visit the Orion spacecraft they will ride to space. (Image credit: NASA/Kim Shiflett) Training for a mission to space is hard work. But sometimes you have to take a minute and have a little fun with your crewmates. What is it? Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding. In the snapshot , the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission. This brief moment of levity took place where the spacecraft currently resides at the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Why is it incredible? This crew has a serious mission ahead of them. The four astronauts will launch to low-Earth orbit around Earth where they plan to practice rendezvous and docking with both Blue Origin and SpaceX's lunar landing vehicles , Blue Moon and Starship, respectively. To prepare, the crew has to undergo months of critical training to both be physically ready while prepared to handle any situation that might come up during their mission. And while Artemis III isn't landing astronauts on the moon, it is a critical step toward that goal. If Artemis III goes to plan and NASA has a lunar landing vehicle that passes rendezvous and docking tests with the Orion spacecraft, Artemis IV might see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

top.description: Jaissle on Newcastle star’s fitness ahead of Brighton Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says Tino Livramento is closing in on a return to the starting XI but insists the club will not rush him back. The defender featured against Arsenal last weekend following his spell out with injury, although Jaissle says a decision on whether he is ready to start has not yet been made, ahead of the game against Brighton. “Always better when we need to make decisions when it comes to the starting XI,” Jaissle said. “Tino, for example, is on his way back but we need to see if he is ready to start. “We still have two days. top.title: Chelsea ramp up interest in Como starlet Jacobo Ramon as Blues make definitive Benoit Badiashile transfer call
top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED - AFP Chelsea are looking to Serie A to bolster their defence in 2027, with Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon emerging as a key target at Stamford Bridge. While the Blues have made a firm decision on Benoit Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli, securing Ramon's signature will require fending off fierce competition from domestic and European rivals. Chelsea plot Serie A defensive overhaul Chelsea are preparing to strengthen their backline in 2027, with their recruitment strategy strongly tied to Serie A. According to The Athletic , the Blues are closely tracking Como centre-back Ramon as they look to add defensive reinforcements. Despite their plans to bolster the squad at the back, Chelsea have no intention of cutting short Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli. The club have decided against recalling any of their first-team loanees during the January transfer window. Rising star Ramon attracts major interest Ramon has caught the eye of decision-makers at Stamford Bridge, where the Spaniard is strongly admired. His impressive progress in Italy was recently rewarded with his first senior call-up to the Spanish national team . Chelsea are not the only English club keeping a close watch on the defender's development. Premier League rivals Arsenal and Manchester United have also been linked with Ramon in recent weeks, pointing towards a potentially competitive race for his signature. Real Madrid hurdle and Badiashile's Napoli stint Any club hoping to prise Ramon away from Como will have to navigate a notable complication. Although he is formally a Como player, Madrid hold an option to re-sign him at the end of the season, mirroring the arrangement they have in place for his team-mate Nico Paz. Meanwhile, Badiashile remains in Italy after moving to Napoli on loan last summer with a €27 million option to buy. The 25-year-old French defender has made five appearances across all competitions this season. Badiashile's campaign was recently interrupted by an injury that sidelined him for several weeks. However, he has now returned to group training with the Serie A side. Summer window key for Chelsea's defensive plans Chelsea supporters will have to remain patient regarding any potential move for Ramon. While the club admire the Como centre-back, a deal would only be possible in the summer transfer window rather than mid-season. With no January recalls planned for Badiashile or any other first-team loanees, the Blues will keep their current loan arrangements intact for the rest of the campaign. Attention will then turn to the summer market, where the Blues' pursuit of Ramon - and the interest from Arsenal, Manchester United, and Madrid - will come into sharper focus.

top.title: Ex-Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jonsson who was part of Euro 2016 squad that stunned England dies aged 37
top.description: Ingvar Jonsson, the former Iceland goalkeeper who was part of the squad that defeated England at the 2016 European Championship, has died at the age of 37. His former club Víkingur announced his death on Thursday. The team did not provide a cause of death, although Jonsson had reportedly been diagnosed with cancer earlier this year. In a statement, the Icelandic club said: "It is with great sorrow and deep sadness that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jonsson, goalkeeper for Víkingur, passed away on Wednesday, November 25, in the arms of his loved ones." They added: "The club and all of Víkingur are thinking of his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences." Jonsson served as an unused substitute during Euro 2016 , when Iceland created one of the greatest shocks in tournament history by knocking England out in the round of 16. The team were later eliminated by France in the quarter-finals. Iceland stunned England at Euro 2016 (Jonathan Brady/PA) (PA Wire) Paying tribute on X, European football’s governing body Uefa wrote: "We extend our deepest condolences to Ingvar’s family, friends and former team-mates. Our thoughts are with them at this difficult time." Jonsson earned eight international caps for Iceland, having made his first squad back in 2012. He had to wait another two years before making his first appearance for his country in a friendly against Belgium. His final cap for Iceland came in 2019, but he continued to make the squad through until 2022. His club career saw him start at Njardvik in his homeland before moving to Norwegian outfit IK Start in 2015. He would go on to play for Sandnes Ulf and Sandefjord prior to leaving Norway in 2018 to join Danish side Viborg. After two years in Denmark, Jonsson returned to Iceland to play for Vikingur and remained at the club until his passing.

top.title: Padres May Have Edge In Seiya Suzuki Chase
top.description: Free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki The San Diego Padres could use help in the outfield, and Seiya Suzuki makes sense as a target. Suzuki and Randy Arozarena are the two best hitters in free agency, and either one would be a great fit for the Padres. However, Arozarena reportedly prefers to sign on the East Coast. The Padres have reportedly shown interest in signing Suzuki, and according to Sanspo Japan , San Diego may have an edge over other suitors. "San Diego is one of the most comfortable environments for Seiya and his wife, Airi," a source told Sanspo Japan. Before Suzuki signed with the Chicago Cubs, the Padres were reportedly a potential landing spot for him. In fact, the Padres may have been his preferred choice. "If the salary and contract terms were the same for multiple interested teams, he would choose the Padres," a source told Sanspo Japan at the time. Suzuki has posted an OPS over .800 in each of the last four years, and was a great defender last year. He was a Gold Glove finalist, after defense had been a flaw in his game for years. The Padres could sign him to play right field and move Fernando Tatis Jr. to left field. They could also try to move Suzuki to left field, but it may not be wise to mess with his defense after he finally figured it out. top.title: Deportivo coach wary of Barcelona quality ahead of La Liga clash: ‘We are going to have to suffer a lot’
top.description: Deportivo coach wary of Barcelona quality ahead of La Liga clash: ‘We are going to have to suffer a lot’ Following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League, Barcelona will resume their La Liga campaign this weekend as they take on Deportivo de A Coruna. It promises to be a tricky affair for the Catalans, having made a long journey to Baku in midweek, forcing Hansi Flick to make multiple changes to the squad. Speaking ahead of the clash, Deportivo coach Antonio Hidalgo talked about the prospect of facing Barcelona and how the team has evolved under Flick. Hidalgo wary of Barcelona Hidalgo started by giving utmost respect to Barcelona, calling them among the finest while praising the standards instilled by Flick. “Surely comes one of the best teams in the world,” he said. “I think Hansi has taken them to a very high level of competitiveness. They’re showing it every week.” “They have won all their matches except one against Madrid and the Champions League against PSG and with an average of four goals per game,” he added. Hidalgo has immense respect for Barcelona. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) The Deportivo coach had no doubts about the challenge waiting for his players, as he demanded total commitment from his team. “We know that we are going to have to suffer a lot without the ball, be very tight. We have to be willing to suffer, to compete at the highest level in all duels and be very intense ,” he added. Hidalgo on Barcelona’s key threat Hidalgo went on to talk about the intensity Barcelona show when out of possession. He singled out that counter-press as a key threat for Deportivo de A Coruna. “We know of the aggressiveness that Barça has without the ball, it puts you a lot of difficulty, especially in that robbery after loss they do,” he said. Despite the challenge, Hidalgo backed his home fans to provide the atmosphere and inspire his players. “With our fans we will be much more powerful, we know it . You always come out with the conviction of competing for matches. “ We are First Division teams and everything is equal. It will be a game of a lot of tension and we will have to compete it at the highest level ,” he said. Aubameyang is expected to feature against former club Barcelona this weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Hidalgo on Barcelona past and Aubameyang relief The match carries personal significance for Hidalgo, who spent his early years in Barcelona’s academy. “I’m from Barcelona, from Canovelles, which is half an hour away. I have my whole family there. From 12 to 21 years old, I was in the Barça quarry,” he said. “When you face teams from that entity, you always see them in a different and special way ,” he added. Finally, Hidalgo confirmed that Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, the former Barcelona forward, is fine after being left unharmed in a car crash ahead of the game. Source: Mundo Deportivo

top.title: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans
top.description: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans Mauricio Pochettino has said it is common sense for him to be involved in Manchester United 's recruitment plans. Manchester United are expected to invest in the January transfer window, as the club look to turn around their campaign. United are currently 19th in the Premier League table after 11 games. A centre-forward and additional defensive depth are understood to be on the agenda for the winter window, which will re-open on January 1, 2027. Pochettino was appointed as head coach on a two-and-a-half year deal this month, and was asked about potential signings on Friday. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Brentford, Pochettino said it would make little sense for him not to be prominent in recruitment plans. "In the future of course, but right now we are focused on trying to relate all of the ideas to the squad," Pochettino said when asked how he will work with the club's leadership. "It's not common sense if the head coach is not involved in situations that affect the build up of the squad. For me, that is a benefit for Manchester United. If I am not involved, and I coach players that you don't know or maybe you don't want, or you don't agree, that is not for me. top.title: ‘Would you approach LeBron James the same way?’ – A’ja Wilson’s agent calls out brands
top.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, has opened up about pushing brands to recognise who Wilson is. A’ja Wilson just locked up a record fifth WNBA MVP, her third in a row, after putting up 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.9 blocks on 52.7% shooting, before the Aces ran into Golden State in the semifinals. While she’s making $1.4 million on the court with Las Vegas, Forbes estimates she’s pulling in over $5 million off it from deals with Nike, Chase, AT&T, and more, showing how big the gap can still be between WNBA salaries and star endorsement money. A’ja Wilson’s agent demands more from brands Even as A’ja Wilson ’s commercial pull keeps growing, her agent says getting brands to truly meet her at her level hasn’t always been simple, pushing companies to see who she is as a Black woman and measure every pitch against how they’d treat an icon like LeBron James . In a recent interview with Forbes , A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, said she has had to have “difficult conversations” with brands to make sure they “understand who she is as a Black woman.” English says she asks them, “‘Would you go to a LeBron James and approach a partnership with him the same way that you would approach A’ja Wilson?’” LeBron James is pulling in $85 million off the court this season, sitting fourth overall in NBA earnings at $88.9 million, with just $3.9 million coming from his salary. Because the NBA has been bigger and around way longer than the WNBA, its stars have had more time to build massive global reach and brand value, which helps explain why James’s off-court haul beats what even top WNBA names make. top.title: Antonelli leads Russell in Qatar first practice
top.description: Kimi Antonelli secured his maiden F1 title in Mexico City earlier this month [Getty Images] World champion Kimi Antonelli headed Mercedes team-mate George Russell in first practice at the penultimate race of the season in Qatar. The 20-year-old Italian posted his fastest time of 1:23.217 on the medium tyre, while Russell's marker, 0.507 seconds adrift, was set on the soft compound. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar finished third, more than six tenths back on Antonelli, with McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri fourth and fifth, 0.850 and 0.860 seconds back. Four-time world champion Max Verstappen ended his session three places lower than team-mate Hadjar in sixth, almost a second off the pace, and complained of shaking on the rear axle of his car. Drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at the Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix on Sunday, which starts at 16:00 GMT. Russell says Verstappen's criticism 'quite amusing' Ferrari facing 'very challenging times' - Hamilton The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed, 16-corner track. Laps to the grid, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included. Lewis Hamilton asked his Ferrari pit wall if anyone else experienced tyre degradation "because mine is massive", to which his engineer replied: "Yes, much higher than expected on all compounds." Hamilton smashed into a marker board during the opening hour in Qatar, while Aston Martin's Lance Stroll, the Williams of Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon plus Gasly also had moments off the dusty track. Charles Leclerc was seventh quickest, one place above Scuderia team-mate Hamilton, with Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad and the Alpine of Pierre Gasly completing the top 10 in ninth and 10th. Red Bull were running different specifications of front wing in first practice as they continue their investigation into what caused Hadjar's failure during last weekend's race in Las Vegas. nigeria.title: Meet Ime Udoka, Nigerian-American coach leading Houston Rockets in the NBA
nigeria.description: Nigerian-American basketball coach Ime Udoka has built an impressive career in basketball, rising from representing Nigeria on the international stage to coaching some of the biggest teams in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Udoka, who currently serves as head coach of the Houston Rockets, has established himself as one of the prominent coaching figures in American basketball, with a career shaped by years of playing, coaching and leadership experience. Born on August 9, 1977, in Portland, Oregon, United States, Udoka has Nigerian roots and represented Nigeria in international basketball competitions before transitioning into coaching. His playing career included spells in the NBA, the NBA Development League and professional basketball leagues in Europe. He also played for Nigeria at the 2005 and 2011 FIBA AfroBasket tournaments, helping raise the country’s profile in international basketball. After retiring from professional basketball, Udoka moved into coaching, beginning his NBA coaching career as an assistant with the San Antonio Spurs in 2012. He worked under legendary coach Gregg Popovich, gaining experience in player development, team management and tactical preparation. During his time with San Antonio, the Spurs reached the NBA Finals in 2013 and won the championship in 2014, providing Udoka with valuable experience at the highest level of the sport. He subsequently served as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets before joining the Boston Celtics in 2021. Led Boston Celtics to NBA Finals Udoka’s breakthrough as a head coach came in 2021 when he was appointed to lead the Boston Celtics. In his first season, he guided the team to the 2022 NBA Finals, where they faced the Golden State Warriors. Although Boston lost the series 4-2, Udoka earned recognition for transforming the team’s defensive performance and guiding its players through a successful playoff campaign. His achievement made him one of the few coaches to reach the NBA Finals in his first season as a head coach. However, his tenure in Boston ended in September 2022 when the franchise suspended him for the 2022–23 season over violations of team policies. New chapter with Houston Rockets In April 2023, the Houston Rockets appointed Udoka as their head coach, giving him another opportunity to lead an NBA franchise. He took charge of a rebuilding team that had struggled in previous seasons and was tasked with improving its competitiveness through tactical discipline, player development and stronger defensive organisation. His appointment marked another significant milestone in his coaching career, as he became responsible for developing a young Houston squad and guiding the franchise towards sustained success. Udoka’s coaching approach has been associated with defensive intensity, accountability and high expectations for players. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s future depends on mentally resilient youths — Mamora
nigeria.description: Former minister urges graduates to embrace purpose, adaptability, continuous learning By Adeola Badru Former Minister of Health, Olorunnimbe Mamora, has said Nigeria’s future depends largely on the mental resilience, character development and sense of purpose of its youths, warning that academic qualifications alone are insufficient to prepare them for the challenges of the modern world. Mamora said young Nigerians must develop the capacity to navigate economic uncertainties, technological disruptions and changing employment opportunities through adaptability, continuous learning and problem-solving skills. He spoke while delivering the 18th Convocation Lecture of Ajayi Crowther University (ACU), Oyo, titled, “Youths’ Mental Health and Purpose: Thriving in a Volatile World.” The former minister challenged graduating students to look beyond the certificates they had earned and prepare for a world where success would increasingly depend on their ability to manage uncertainty, identify opportunities and remain relevant. He described convocation as a transition into a new phase of life, requiring graduates to demonstrate resilience, discipline, adaptability and a clear sense of purpose. Mamora identified the growing influence of social media, economic pressures and rapid technological advancement as emerging challenges to the mental wellbeing of young people. While acknowledging that the internet had expanded access to information and opportunities, he noted that excessive engagement with digital platforms could contribute to loneliness, anxiety and unhealthy comparisons. He urged graduates not to measure their achievements or personal worth against the lifestyles and apparent successes of others on social media. “Do not allow social media platforms to become the mirror through which you measure your worth. “Your value is not determined by the number of people who like your photograph. Stop comparing your backstage with somebody else’s stage,” he said. On the changing employment landscape, particularly with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Mamora said graduates must recognise that education should go beyond acquiring academic qualifications. He stressed the importance of critical thinking, problem-solving, skills acquisition and continuous learning, noting that adaptability would be essential to remaining relevant in the evolving world of work. nigeria.title: Omo-Agege denies snubbing police invitation over Uduere killings
nigeria.description: Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has denied reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. In a statement on Friday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the former Deputy President of the Senate said he had seen the reports and described them as untrue. “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has seen the reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. “It isn’t true. You can’t turn down an invitation you never received,” he said. According to the statement, no formal invitation has reached the Senator or his office. “No letter has reached the Senator or his office, and no officer has come to him with one. He first learned of it the same way everyone else did, from the Command’s announcement in the media.” Areh said the report that Omo-Agege refused to appear was based on a single unnamed source. “The claim that he refused leans on a single unnamed source. The Senator hasn’t told the police, or anyone else, that he won’t appear.” The statement also revisited the events at Uduere, insisting that Omo-Agege was the victim of the attack. “It is worth remembering what happened at Uduere. Senator Omo-Agege was the target of an assassination attempt. Senior members of his campaign team were murdered, and others are still in hospital with serious injuries. “He is the one who survived an attack on his life, and the one demanding that those responsible be found and prosecuted.” Omo-Agege said he wants the case resolved and justice for the victims. “He wants this case resolved, and he wants justice for the dead and the wounded. If the police serve a lawful invitation, he will honour it. He asks only that it be sent through his office so a date can be agreed.” He faulted the manner in which the alleged invitation was made public. “A summons announced in the press before it reaches the person named is not due process, and he won’t be tried in the media,” he said. nigeria.title: Full list: African countries where travelers can access without visa
nigeria.description: Travelling across Africa is becoming easier as more countries adopt visa-free entry policies aimed at promoting tourism, strengthening regional integration and encouraging trade among African nations. Several African countries have introduced policies allowing citizens of other African countries to visit without obtaining a visa before travelling, reducing the cost and administrative hurdles associated with cross-border movement. Among the countries offering such access are Benin, The Gambia, Rwanda, Seychelles, Ghana and Togo. The policies form part of wider efforts to improve freedom of movement across the continent and advance the African Union’s goal of greater economic integration. The six countries are highlighted below, although their entry arrangements are not identical. 1. Benin Benin is one of Africa’s leading supporters of visa-free movement. It allows citizens of other African countries to enter without obtaining a visa before travelling. The country has promoted easier cross-border movement to encourage tourism, business and regional cooperation. 2. The Gambia The Gambia offers visa-free entry to citizens of other African countries. It is one of the continent’s more open destinations, making it attractive to visitors interested in tourism, business and cultural exchanges. 3. Rwanda Rwanda allows citizens of African Union member states to enter without a visa. The policy supports the country’s efforts to attract African visitors, investors and business travellers. 4. Seychelles Seychelles operates a visa-free entry policy for visitors of all nationalities, including African travellers. However, visitors must obtain the required travel authorisation before departure and meet the country’s entry conditions. 5. Ghana Ghana introduced a free visa policy for African nationals in May 2026. Under the arrangement, African travellers can apply for electronic visas without paying visa fees. However, an application and approval are still required, meaning the policy is not strictly visa-free entry. 6. Togo Togo has introduced visa-free entry for African passport holders, subject to pre-arrival requirements. The policy is part of efforts to facilitate movement across the continent and strengthen regional integration. nigeria.title: Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim that boxer has schizophrenia
nigeria.description: Paris Fury, the wife of British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury, has withdrawn her earlier claim that her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying that he has never been formally diagnosed with the condition. Paris made the clarification after an earlier version of an upcoming Netflix documentary about the boxer featured her describing him as having “mild schizophrenia”. In a statement, she said she had used the term while recalling a conversation about Tyson’s mental health struggles several years ago, but acknowledged that it was not an accurate description of his medical history. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” she said. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” She added that mental health was complex and that finding the right words to describe someone’s experiences was not always easy. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love,” she said. Paris also praised her husband for speaking openly about his struggles and thanked the public for supporting their family. Netflix confirmed that it had updated the documentary following the family’s clarification about Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis. “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch,” the streaming platform said. The earlier comments had attracted attention from the British Boxing Board of Control, which indicated that it was investigating the matter. The 38 year old boxer is scheduled to face Joshua in an all British heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11, with the vacant WBA title expected to be at stake. Tyson has previously spoken publicly about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, when he became world heavyweight champion. After the victory, he took a break of nearly three years from boxing, during which he battled suicidal thoughts, drug and alcohol problems, and significant weight gain. Reflecting on that period in the documentary, Tyson said he experienced severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” he said. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” He later returned to boxing and regained the world heavyweight title by defeating Deontay Wilder in February 2020. nigeria.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
nigeria.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. nigeria.title: UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians
nigeria.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case. That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets. Galaxy points to $58,525 The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22. Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself. History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. sports.title: Chelsea ramp up interest in Como starlet Jacobo Ramon as Blues make definitive Benoit Badiashile transfer call
sports.description: FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED - AFP Chelsea are looking to Serie A to bolster their defence in 2027, with Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon emerging as a key target at Stamford Bridge. While the Blues have made a firm decision on Benoit Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli, securing Ramon's signature will require fending off fierce competition from domestic and European rivals. Chelsea plot Serie A defensive overhaul Chelsea are preparing to strengthen their backline in 2027, with their recruitment strategy strongly tied to Serie A. According to The Athletic , the Blues are closely tracking Como centre-back Ramon as they look to add defensive reinforcements. Despite their plans to bolster the squad at the back, Chelsea have no intention of cutting short Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli. The club have decided against recalling any of their first-team loanees during the January transfer window. Rising star Ramon attracts major interest Ramon has caught the eye of decision-makers at Stamford Bridge, where the Spaniard is strongly admired. His impressive progress in Italy was recently rewarded with his first senior call-up to the Spanish national team . Chelsea are not the only English club keeping a close watch on the defender's development. Premier League rivals Arsenal and Manchester United have also been linked with Ramon in recent weeks, pointing towards a potentially competitive race for his signature. Real Madrid hurdle and Badiashile's Napoli stint Any club hoping to prise Ramon away from Como will have to navigate a notable complication. Although he is formally a Como player, Madrid hold an option to re-sign him at the end of the season, mirroring the arrangement they have in place for his team-mate Nico Paz. Meanwhile, Badiashile remains in Italy after moving to Napoli on loan last summer with a €27 million option to buy. The 25-year-old French defender has made five appearances across all competitions this season. Badiashile's campaign was recently interrupted by an injury that sidelined him for several weeks. However, he has now returned to group training with the Serie A side. Summer window key for Chelsea's defensive plans Chelsea supporters will have to remain patient regarding any potential move for Ramon. While the club admire the Como centre-back, a deal would only be possible in the summer transfer window rather than mid-season. With no January recalls planned for Badiashile or any other first-team loanees, the Blues will keep their current loan arrangements intact for the rest of the campaign. sports.title: Ex-Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jonsson who was part of Euro 2016 squad that stunned England dies aged 37
sports.description: Ingvar Jonsson, the former Iceland goalkeeper who was part of the squad that defeated England at the 2016 European Championship, has died at the age of 37. His former club Víkingur announced his death on Thursday. The team did not provide a cause of death, although Jonsson had reportedly been diagnosed with cancer earlier this year. In a statement, the Icelandic club said: "It is with great sorrow and deep sadness that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jonsson, goalkeeper for Víkingur, passed away on Wednesday, November 25, in the arms of his loved ones." They added: "The club and all of Víkingur are thinking of his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences." Jonsson served as an unused substitute during Euro 2016 , when Iceland created one of the greatest shocks in tournament history by knocking England out in the round of 16. The team were later eliminated by France in the quarter-finals. Iceland stunned England at Euro 2016 (Jonathan Brady/PA) (PA Wire) Paying tribute on X, European football’s governing body Uefa wrote: "We extend our deepest condolences to Ingvar’s family, friends and former team-mates. Our thoughts are with them at this difficult time." Jonsson earned eight international caps for Iceland, having made his first squad back in 2012. He had to wait another two years before making his first appearance for his country in a friendly against Belgium. His final cap for Iceland came in 2019, but he continued to make the squad through until 2022. His club career saw him start at Njardvik in his homeland before moving to Norwegian outfit IK Start in 2015. He would go on to play for Sandnes Ulf and Sandefjord prior to leaving Norway in 2018 to join Danish side Viborg. After two years in Denmark, Jonsson returned to Iceland to play for Vikingur and remained at the club until his passing.

"If the salary and contract terms were the same for multiple interested teams, he would choose the Padres," a source told Sanspo Japan at the time. Suzuki has posted an OPS over .800 in each of the last four years, and was a great defender last year. He was a Gold Glove finalist, after defense had been a flaw in his game for years. sports.title: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans
sports.description: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans Mauricio Pochettino has said it is common sense for him to be involved in Manchester United 's recruitment plans. Manchester United are expected to invest in the January transfer window, as the club look to turn around their campaign. United are currently 19th in the Premier League table after 11 games. A centre-forward and additional defensive depth are understood to be on the agenda for the winter window, which will re-open on January 1, 2027. Pochettino was appointed as head coach on a two-and-a-half year deal this month, and was asked about potential signings on Friday. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Brentford, Pochettino said it would make little sense for him not to be prominent in recruitment plans. "In the future of course, but right now we are focused on trying to relate all of the ideas to the squad," Pochettino said when asked how he will work with the club's leadership. "It's not common sense if the head coach is not involved in situations that affect the build up of the squad. For me, that is a benefit for Manchester United. If I am not involved, and I coach players that you don't know or maybe you don't want, or you don't agree, that is not for me. "I respect all ways to work but I am going to take my responsibility and everyone is going to know that I am going to be involved. That is what we were talking [about] in the last few days. "Being the coach is not only to pick 11 players. It's to assess and analyse the work behind about how you build. The responsibility is massive from the coaching staff." Manchester United have addressed one squad issue by activating a one-year extension in Bruno Fernandes' contract. Fernandes' deal was due to expire in the summer but has been extended until 2028.

sports.title: ‘Would you approach LeBron James the same way?’ – A’ja Wilson’s agent calls out brands
sports.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, has opened up about pushing brands to recognise who Wilson is. A’ja Wilson just locked up a record fifth WNBA MVP, her third in a row, after putting up 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.9 blocks on 52.7% shooting, before the Aces ran into Golden State in the semifinals. While she’s making $1.4 million on the court with Las Vegas, Forbes estimates she’s pulling in over $5 million off it from deals with Nike, Chase, AT&T, and more, showing how big the gap can still be between WNBA salaries and star endorsement money. A’ja Wilson’s agent demands more from brands Even as A’ja Wilson ’s commercial pull keeps growing, her agent says getting brands to truly meet her at her level hasn’t always been simple, pushing companies to see who she is as a Black woman and measure every pitch against how they’d treat an icon like LeBron James . In a recent interview with Forbes , A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, said she has had to have “difficult conversations” with brands to make sure they “understand who she is as a Black woman.” English says she asks them, “‘Would you go to a LeBron James and approach a partnership with him the same way that you would approach A’ja Wilson?’” LeBron James is pulling in $85 million off the court this season, sitting fourth overall in NBA earnings at $88.9 million, with just $3.9 million coming from his salary. Because the NBA has been bigger and around way longer than the WNBA, its stars have had more time to build massive global reach and brand value, which helps explain why James’s off-court haul beats what even top WNBA names make. sports.title: Fabrizio Romano: Liverpool ‘already discussing’ next steps under Andoni Iraola
sports.description: Fabrizio Romano: Liverpool ‘already discussing’ next steps under Andoni Iraola Andoni Iraola Earning Liverpool Trust as Long Term Planning Begins Liverpool have moved quickly to stabilise the mood around Anfield, and the early signs under Andoni Iraola are encouraging. According to Fabrizio Romano, the club’s senior figures are pleased with what they have seen from the new head coach, and that matters because this is about more than a decent run of results. It is about direction, authority and whether Liverpool finally look coherent again. Romano’s key line was clear: “They are already discussing with Andoni Iraola about future plans and what they want to do. They are delighted with the coach and the coach is delighted with the Liverpool project. [He has] very good connections with the players.” That tells you two things. First, there is internal alignment. Second, this is not being treated as a short term fix. Liverpool Results Show Real Progress It has been close to six months since Iraola replaced Arne Slot, and the numbers are solid. Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League, just one point off second, they are well placed to reach the Champions League last 16 automatically, and they are through to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals. Add in penalty shootouts and he has won 12 of his first 18 matches, with only three defeats. Those figures do not prove anything on their own, but they do show competence, and after the chaos of the end of last season, competence is a serious improvement. Liverpool look sharper, more connected and more purposeful. There is structure in and out of possession, and there is less of the drift that damaged the side previously. Andoni Iraola Impact on Key Players The biggest positive may be individual improvement. Alexander Isak looks increasingly decisive, Florian Wirtz is influencing games with more regularity, and Alexis Mac Allister appears refreshed after a difficult end to the previous campaign. When Liverpool’s best players are performing like elite players, the whole team changes shape. This is where coaches earn credibility. Tactical ideas are fine, but players need to look better under your management than they did before. Right now, several Liverpool players do. That is why the praise from inside the club carries weight. Transfer Plans Already Point to Stability Iraola only signed a two-year deal, which raised eyebrows at the time. In reality, that suited his track record and suited a club that had just been burned badly. Shorter contracts can still produce long term thinking if both sides are convinced by the process. The fact discussions are already taking place over transfer plans for 2027 and beyond suggests Liverpool believe they have found a coach worth building with. That does not guarantee anything by spring. Football moves fast, and reputations collapse quickly when results turn. But for now, Liverpool have a head coach improving players, collecting wins and restoring order. That is a very good start.

technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

technology.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
technology.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. "We have taken some DWP online services offline as a precaution after we identified a cyber incident affecting our systems," it said. "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre (GC3) to investigate and to bring services back online as quickly as possible and to minimize any disruption. "Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal. If an online service you need is unavailable, please try again later. As always, we will never message you to ask for bank details or ask you to click on links." The Register contacted both the DWP and NCSC for more information. The DWP declined to comment beyond the statement issued publicly. GC3 coordinates responses to incidents affecting government. The Government Cyber Unit leads the wider Government Cyber Action Plan, backed by more than £210 million. It is led by the government CISO, Bella Powell. Officials have not commented on any of the usual details one would expect from a cyber incident disclosure, including the specific services that were downed, when they are expected to return, or whether any data is thought to be compromised, even at this early stage. technology.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

technology.title: Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids
